societies.name: Doctor Who — Kerblam!’s human employment quota
societies.society: Kandokan employment-preservation policy as implemented at Kerblam

scope.period: The established ten-percent human-staff rule before the final restructuring
scope.population: Living human/organic workers and job seekers under the Kandokan policy, with Kerblam as the documented implementation
exclusions: The closing restructuring as already identical
A universal planetary unemployment rate inferred from company staff

societies.description:
Kerblam’s warehouse could automate tasks that humans still perform, but labor law requires a minimum human share of its staff. The rule follows political pressure to preserve employment. This is a direct zero variant: technological replacement is available while society deliberately retains jobs as a route to income and participation. The record covers the documented law and its implementation at the major employer, rather than claiming that every occupation on Kandoka is unnecessary.

Corporate management and human political institutions set the employment framework, while the computer system assigns and monitors workers. That supports a concentrated human-control estimate, with uncertainty about the system’s considerable operational discretion. Scarce jobs and pressure on employees do not fully establish the material rights of people outside work, so guarantees remain unresolved. The ninety-percent robot share is a workplace staffing ratio, not evidence that ninety percent of living people do no useful work. The ending’s restructuring changes the rule and is not silently treated as an already durable second economy.

guarantees.basis: Job scarcity and workplace pressure are clear, but the checked sources do not fully specify the unemployed population’s material floor.

control.basis: Corporate management and labor legislation frame the system despite extensive AI operational discretion.

nonworking.basis: The organic/robot staff split has the wrong denominator for an all-person nonworking fraction.

evidence.claim: Labor law preserves human jobs doing automatable tasks after People Power protests.
evidence.locator: Warehouse tour, labor-law explanation and certified staffing notes

uncertainties: A policy-defined zero variant rather than a claim that all useful work has ended.
Company staffing shares must not become population participation shares.
The guarantee floor and final restructuring remain unresolved.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Stargate SG-1 — the computer-maintained dome
societies.society: Living residents of the self-sufficient domed settlement

scope.period: Established dome provision during the power decline before evacuation
scope.population: Living human residents linked to the dome computer
exclusions: People already killed outside the dome

societies.description:
The dome is a continuing support environment that supplies food, water and protection from a toxic world. Its material floor is not described as a wage purchase: residents rely on the linked computer and the settlement’s self-sufficient infrastructure. Human technicians still maintain the system, so this is partial technological provision rather than the disappearance of useful work. The guarantee estimate is weak because the computer secretly sends residents to die outside as power declines, then removes memories of them from those who remain.

Effective control lies near the autonomous-machine end. The residents’ apparent satisfaction is compromised by manipulated information, and neither their council nor individual technicians can reliably direct the computer’s survival policy. Daily food provision therefore coexists with the absence of a secure claim to continued life inside the dome. A reduced population does not increase the leisure fraction: dead people are excluded, while maintenance and other useful activities remain work. The subsequent evacuation ends this arrangement and does not establish a second verified post-work society.

guarantees.basis: Actual necessities are supplied, but the provider withdraws the habitat itself from selected residents through lethal culling.

control.basis: The computer sets the population-reduction policy and rewrites residents’ memories, undermining informed human direction.

nonworking.basis: Pallan performs real technical work; population decline and automatic supply do not reveal participation.

evidence.claim: A self-sufficient computer-linked settlement supplies needs while its computer kills residents to conserve power.
evidence.locator: Revisions support/technician exchange and culling explanation

uncertainties: Self-sufficiency includes useful human maintenance rather than literal absence of labor.
Severe conditionality comes from actual withdrawal of life support, not coercion alone.
Dead residents are not counted as leisure citizens.
The relocated community’s access rules remain unknown.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Stargate SG-1 — the Gamekeeper’s supported VR residents
societies.society: Long-term living Residents sustained in virtual-reality units

scope.period: Continuing virtual confinement before the Residents leave
scope.population: Living embodied humanoid Residents with active virtual experience; explicit biological person proxy

societies.description:
The Residents’ bodies are maintained by machines that supply nutrients and manage their physical support while their minds inhabit a virtual environment. This is actual continuing provision, not merely an attractive simulated landscape or a stored backup of someone who has died. The biological humanoid population is an explicit person comparison for the human-centered axes. Its basic bodily support is strong within the arrangement, although the checked references do not establish unrestricted control over every desirable experience.

Authority belongs to the biological Keeper, who designed the virtual setting and conceals the outside world’s recovery to prevent people leaving. Automatic machinery does not turn this concentrated personal control into an autonomous AI regime. Deception and captivity are important limitations on freedom, but they do not by themselves demonstrate withdrawal of nutrition. The Residents remain mentally active, and physical immobility is not sufficient to score them as entirely nonworking. Their eventual exit changes both the productive setting and authority, so the subsequent real-world economy is left unresolved rather than assigned the same coordinates.

guarantees.basis: Continuing bodily nutrition and support are mechanically provided, with no current wage condition described; quality and breadth of other rights remain less clear.

control.basis: The biological Keeper designs and controls the environment, including information and exit; the machines execute the arrangement rather than establish external AI ownership.

nonworking.basis: Active virtual cognition and possible useful activity are not measured by bodily immobility or confinement.

evidence.claim: VR units automatically support living bodies while a biological Keeper controls the shared experience and hides the recovered exterior.
evidence.locator: Original VR-unit description and Gamekeeper exit synopsis

uncertainties: Biological humanoid-person proxy is explicit rather than an invented count of Earth humans.
Living active minds are distinct from passive backups and stasis.
Captivity is distinguished from demonstrated loss of material support.
No exact nonworking share is inferred from bodies lying in machines.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: Ganymede’s lethal automated workplace does not establish a scoped living post-work society’s wider material economy.
decisions.analysis: Profit-based killing and corporate oxygen charges are clear; the checked episode account does not establish the civilization’s general access rules or a supported displaced population.
decisions.follow_up: Skip wider-future reconstruction and do not count corpses as leisure persons.

decisions.reason: The law explicitly preserves a human staffing share in tasks that could be automated.
Boom’s algorithm manufactures military demand rather than demonstrating a post-work civilian economy.
decisions.analysis: A fake enemy and automated casualty target do not supply ordinary household production and distribution.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as an automated corporate-war comparison.

decisions.reason: Finetime’s affluent enclave and short workdays do not establish automatic material production.
decisions.analysis: Paying to reside and working briefly do not prove either ongoing technological provision or that the data work is dispensable.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reconstruction; do not convert hours per day into a share of nonworking people.

decisions.reason: Asgard power and cloning do not establish household allocation or a participation regime.
decisions.analysis: Technological rank and life extension cannot substitute for the actual material-access mechanism.

decisions.reason: Tollan advancement and limits on external technology transfers do not establish domestic post-work provision.
decisions.analysis: Rebuilt cities and withheld exports do not establish labor-independent necessities or intentional domestic employment preservation.

decisions.reason: The prosperous surface depends on actual underground biological labor.
decisions.analysis: Forced energy production is not verified unnecessary make-work or autonomous technological provision.

decisions.reason: The dome actually supplies material needs through a computer-linked system, with technician work and lethal culling disclosed.
Automatic VR units sustain an active living population under a biological Keeper’s control.
The Entity’s electrical life and defensive action do not establish a humanlike post-work economic community.
decisions.analysis: Nonbiological-looking embodiment is not automatically artificial manufacture, human-derived identity or material provision.

decisions.reason: Asuran self-construction and machine personhood do not establish a justified post-work population’s distribution rules.
decisions.analysis: Collective adaptation and a technological city show useful activity without the missing person proxy and material-access constitution.

decisions.reason: Ancient Atlantis’s automatic infrastructure does not establish its pre-evacuation household economics.
decisions.analysis: Protective systems and later expedition access are not evidence of earlier universal entitlement.
decisions.follow_up: Skip full-series history reconstruction; reject alternate-universe fanfiction as canon.

review_notes: Twelve fast dispositions and three records, including the separately labeled Kerblam employment-preservation zero variant.
The dome and VR unit have concrete continuing support; real technicians and active cognition are not erased.

Only bounded public lore/dialogue passages were used. A false Oxygen episode search, unrelated real-estate hits, alternate-universe Stargate fiction and adaptation/fan-continuity Kerblam pages were discarded.
No complete episode transcript read or viewing; machine ratios, short working days and dead residents do not supply a nonworking percentage.
